record.paper_title: Open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems
record.original_question: If a measure-preserving dynamical system is Kakutani realizable by a smooth toral system, must it also be realizable up to measure isomorphism?

evidence.quote: Question 5.3 (Rodriguez Hertz). If a measure-preserving system is Kakutani realizable can we conclude it is also isomorphically realizable?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(X,\mathcal{B},\mu,T)$ be an invertible measure-preserving dynamical system on a standard probability space. Recall:

- Two measure-preserving systems $(X,\mu,T)$ and $(Y,\nu,S)$ are said to be *measure isomorphic* if there exist full-measure invariant subsets $X_0\subseteq X$, $Y_0\subseteq Y$ and a measurable bijection $\phi:X_0\to Y_0$ with $\phi_*\mu=\nu$ and $\phi\circ T=S\circ\phi$ on $X_0$.
- Two systems are *Kakutani equivalent* if each is measure isomorphic to a measurable induced (first-return) transformation of the other on some positive-measure subset; equivalently, they admit isomorphic suspension flows up to time change.
- A measure-preserving system $(X,\mu,T)$ is said to be *smoothly realizable on the torus* (isomorphically) if there exist $d\geq 1$, a $C^\infty$ diffeomorphism $f:\mathbb{T}^d\to\mathbb{T}^d$, and an $f$-invariant Borel probability measure $\nu$ on $\mathbb{T}^d$ such that $(\mathbb{T}^d,\nu,f)$ is measure isomorphic to $(X,\mu,T)$.
- It is said to be *Kakutani realizable on the torus* if such an $f$ exists with $(\mathbb{T}^d,\nu,f)$ Kakutani equivalent to $(X,\mu,T)$.

Question: If a measure-preserving dynamical system on a standard probability space is Kakutani realizable by a smooth diffeomorphism of some torus equipped with an invariant Borel probability measure, must it also be isomorphically realizable by a smooth diffeomorphism of some torus with an invariant Borel probability measure?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem attributed to F. Rodriguez Hertz in a 2023 survey on open questions in descriptive set theory and dynamical systems. A web search did not surface any subsequent work resolving the smooth-toral Kakutani-vs-isomorphic realization question; related rigidity and realization work by Rodriguez Hertz and collaborators addresses different aspects (e.g., smooth rigidity of Anosov maps), so the problem appears to remain open.
